caption: The drawing depicts a cylindrical stoneware vessel with thick walls and a slightly flared rim at the top. The vessel has two rounded handles on opposite sides near the upper section. The surface of the vessel is mostly a muted grayish color, with visible cracks and a spot suggesting wear or age. Decorative blue floral or foliate patterns adorn the spaces between the handles. Emerging vertically from the vessel's mouth is a cylindrical wooden stick or plunger, which sits inside the vessel. In the upper right corner of the drawing, a smaller, detailed inset shows a close-up of the vessel’s rim, one handle, and a section of the blue decorative motif. The background is a plain, light beige color, with no additional objects or scenery present.
title: Butter Churn
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
